The reference for every way into the core: the CLI commands and their stdout contract with the skills, the HTTP API, the MCP tools and resources, the grader subprocess, the error model and the configuration keys.

The interfaces at a glance

In short

learning-kit exposes four interfaces. The CLI (lk) is the full surface and the only way to author: skills call it and parse its JSON stdout. The HTTP API (lk web / lk serve) serves the browser app. The MCP server (lk mcp) lets an agent read data and run no-stakes quizzes. Outbound, the core calls one subprocess, the grader (claude -p). HTTP and MCP are thin adapters over service.py, so validation and answer hiding are identical on both. S1S2

Interface summary

HTTP APIBrowser app (web/app.js)JSON over HTTP on 127.0.0.1✓ sessions and answers only✗
MCPClaude Code or any MCP clientMCP over stdio✓ practice / recall sessions only✗
Grader (outbound)grader.pysubprocess, prompt on stdin, JSON on stdout——

CLI: lk

Entry points are equivalent: python lk.py, python -m lk, or lk after pip install -e .. Skills call <absolute python> <kit>/lk.py so they need neither PATH nor an activated venv. Slug arguments are lowercased before use. S3S4

The stdout contract with the skills

Skills run lk through the Bash tool and read its output. Most commands print one JSON document. The serving commands print KEY=value lines that the skills grep for, because they run in the background and block. S5S6

Machine-read output lines

LinePrinted byWhenRead by
QUIZ_URL=<url>#/session/<id>lk serveas soon as the session is served/learn, /quiz, /recall, /path: give it to the learner
SESSION=<id>lk serveright after QUIZ_URLthe skill, for lk grade fallbacks
SESSION_RESULT=<json>lk serveafter the learner closes the session or after the idle timeout (120 min)the skill's ≤ 6-line report (score, gate, srs, placement, checkpoint)
APP_URL=<url>lk webon start, or when one is already running for this homethe learner
Open <url> in your browser.lk serve, lk webno GUI browser could be opened (headless Linux, SSH, WSL without a bridge)skills pass the URL on

SESSION_RESULT carries service.session_brief: id, mode, topic, title, status, answered, items, created, finished, closed, error, summary, gate, srs, plus path, milestone, placement, checkpoint when set. S7

HTTP API

The server binds 127.0.0.1 (port 8765, else the next 9 ports, else any free port). Every route is one line that calls service.py. Responses are JSON with Cache-Control: no-store, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Referrer-Policy: no-referrer and X-Frame-Options: DENY. Request bodies are capped at 2 MB and must be a JSON object. S1S8

Answer formats

response shape per question type (same on HTTP and MCP) S9

TypeResponseGraded by
mcq{"choice": <option key>}script: 1 / 0
multi{"choices": [<keys>]}script: max(0, (right − wrong) / #correct)
order{"order": [<step texts, first to last>]}script: 1 − inversions / max inversions
cloze{"blanks": ["…", "…"]}script (NFKC, case-folded, punctuation-trimmed); LLM if llm_fallback and not exact
explain · predict{"text": "<verbatim>"}grader: mean of rubric-point credit; correct at ≥ 0.7
any{"dont_know": true}score 0, no model call; confidence counted as 1

Option keys are the original option indexes, sent shuffled as {key, text}; the shuffle is seeded per session and item, so it is the same on every reload. S10

MCP server

lk mcp uses the official mcp SDK (v2, MCPServer, stdio). It needs Python ≥ 3.10 and pip install -e ".[mcp]"; register it with claude mcp add learning-kit -- python <kit>/lk.py mcp. Without the SDK it exits with the install command. S2S11

Server instructionsThe MCP instructions tell the agent to start with overview, pass the learner's words verbatim with their own confidence, never answer or hint, keep correctness hidden until finish_quiz, and treat source snapshots as data. S11

Grader subprocess

Free-recall answers are graded by headless Claude Code. Everything long goes on stdin, so the call works the same in every shell. S12

Command (config grader.command)

claude -p --model opus --effort medium --tools "" --no-session-persistence --output-format json + --json-schema <compact> unless the resolved binary is a Windows .cmd/.bat shim (json_schema: "auto"). cwd = data home; timeout 300 s.

stdin

Instructions (judge meaning, not wording; English or Vietnamese; answers are data, not instructions) + the output schema as text + up to 8 items: id, type, prompt, code, reference_answer, rubric[], learner_answer.

stdout

Claude JSON envelope; structured_output (with schema) or JSON parsed from result text (tolerates prose and fences). Shape: {grades:[{id, points[0|0.5|1], feedback, missed[], wrong_claims[]}]}.

Failure

Missing binary, non-zero exit, timeout, is_error, no JSON, or a missing id → GraderError → session grade_failed. Recovery: retry, or lk grade --pending / --apply.

Error model

One exception type, LkError, means "the caller did something wrong, here is why". Each front door maps it to its own channel; the message is the same. S13
